title: kv-cache: adaptive spillover + coalescing compaction to reduce fragmentation and OOMs
author: Alex Martinez
description: Motivation: production hosts observed periodic OOMs and degraded throughput under mixed-sequence workloads due to KV cache fragmentation and naive spillover. This PR implements an adaptive spillover + coalescing compaction strategy that reduces live fragmentation, prioritizes hot-key retention, and bounds memory used for spillover paging. The change includes: (1) a background coalescing compaction that merges adjacent free fragments when fragmentation exceeds a tunable threshold, (2) an adaptive spillover allocator that pages cold KV entries to persistent spill files with a configurable hysteresis window to avoid thrash, (3) an eviction priority update that prefers evicting the least recently used large-span fragments and small cold entries differently to minimize wasted space, (4) a lightweight defragmentation work-stealing scheduler to amortize compaction cost across worker threads, and (5) observability additions (fragmentation histograms, spill ratio, compaction latency, pages read/write counters). The description below summarizes the user-visible behavior and operational knobs. Changes are backward-compatible; runtime defaults are conservative and gated behind feature flag KV_COALESCE_V3 to allow staged rollout. Checklist: - [x] design doc (link: internal/linear/ENG-7201) - [x] unit + integration tests - [x] end-to-end perf microbenchmarks (kv-cache heavy mixed workloads) - [x] added observability and dashboard patches - [x] feature-flag gating for controlled rollout Implementation notes: - Coalescing compaction runs when fragmentation_ratio > 0.25 (configurable) and targets contiguous free spans for merging; uses fence-free short pauses to avoid blocking inference threads. - Adaptive spillover uses an LRU-epoch scoring for cold entries; entries with score below threshold are lazily paged out to spill files and rehydrated on access. We bound spill file memory mapping to max_spill_mmap_bytes to avoid excessive RSS. - Eviction now considers "waste_score" = fragmentation_impact * size_factor + recency_penalty; tuning reduces removal of small hot entries that would increase fragmentation. - Work-stealing scheduler ensures background compaction tasks are distributed across inference worker pools to prevent head-of-line latency for new requests. - Added end-to-end smoke tests for rehydrate paths and failure injection to ensure correctness under disk I/O latency. Benchmarks (summary): - Synthetic mixed-sequence workload (seq len distribution 32/128/2048): 95th latency improved 18% under heavy memory pressure; OOMs eliminated in 120h soak tests where previous runtime failed within 6-12h. - Throughput: stable throughput improved 7% on p4d instances due to reduced allocation churn and fewer spill reads. Rollout plan: gate behind KV_COALESCE_V3; run on 10% of Dedicated pools for 48h, then 50% if no regressions, full rollout after 7d. Feature flags and config: - KV_COALESCE_V3=true - kv.coalesce.fragmentation_threshold (default 0.25) - kv.spill.hysteresis_ms (default 500) - kv.spill.max_spill_mmap_bytes (default 256MB) Observability additions: - runtime.kv.fragmentation_ratio (gauge) - runtime.kv.compaction_latency_ms (histogram) - runtime.kv.spill.reads_total (counter) - runtime.kv.spill.writes_total (counter) Backwards compatibility: config defaults prevent aggressive compaction unless enabled. Migration: none required for on-disk spill files; format is forward compatible with a version header. Known issues and follow-ups: - In very low-latency single-request profiles, coalescing introduces small (sub-ms) background CPU; we plan an "aggressive_offload" mode to push compaction to dedicated threads in a follow-up (ENG-7342). - We saw a rare race in early testing around concurrent rehydrate + eviction; fixed in commit that gates rehydrate with a per-entry lock and fallback path. Testing: extensive unit tests for allocator, integration tests for spill paging with mocked disk latency, e2e soak tests in perf-canary. See commits for details.
